title: Affine conormal realization and augmented Jacobian cofactor formula
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $c\geq0$, $P=R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ for an ordered regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $B=P/I$, $C=I/I^2$, $V=\bigoplus_{j=0}^c B\,dx_j$ and $u:C\to V$, $u(\bar f_i)=\sum_j\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j}dx_j$. Differentials mean [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and exterior powers mean [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Write $E=[C\xrightarrow{u}V]$ in degrees $-1,0$ and $D(E)=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes_B\bigwedge^{c+1}V$, with $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B)$. Then $C$ has the indicated conormal basis $\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_c$ and $V$ has basis $dx_0,\ldots,dx_c$. The canonical conormal comparison $E\simeq L_{B/R}$ for the intrinsic cotangent complex of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] is an isomorphism in the derived category, with $D(E)\simeq\det L_{B/R}$ for [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. Its degree-zero identification is the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}u\simeq\Omega^1_{B/R}$ sending the class of $dx_j$ to $d\bar x_j$. There is a unique $B$-linear map $w:\Omega^1_{B/R}\to D(E)$ with
$$w(\bar v)=(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes\bigl(u(\bar f_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(\bar f_c)\wedge v\bigr)$$
for every $v\in V$, where $\bar v$ is its image in the cokernel. This value is independent of the lift $v$ and of the basis used for $C$; it is the cofactor map of [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality]. Let $e_0:D(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ send $(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c)$ to $1$. For every $a\in P$ one has
$$e_0(w(d\bar a))=\overline{\det\!\left(\frac{\partial(f_1,\ldots,f_c,a)}{\partial(x_0,\ldots,x_c)}\right)}.$$
These identifications and formulas commute with restriction to open affine subschemes of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and transport by isomorphisms of the presented $R$-algebras. The orientation is relation-first, as in the kernel-first determinant normalization of the cited cofactor lemma; changing to the corresponding shifted Koszul convention changes the scalar trivialization by a sign depending only on $c$. The assertions include $c=0$, when $C=0$ and $w(dx_0)=dx_0$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula and omitted well-definedness check; cotangent.tex Tags 08SJ, 08SL, conormal model. Extracts old proof steps 1-3 and local transport in step 7; agent-formulated combined local realization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] with ambient ring $P$ and module $P$. Thus the given sequence is Koszul-regular, and [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] gives the basis $p_i=\bar f_i$ of $C=I/I^2$, including the empty basis when $c=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $B\otimes_P\Omega^1_{P/R}$ is the displayed free module $V$ on $dx_0,\ldots,dx_c$. In these coordinates the conormal differential is $u(p_i)=\sum_j\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j}dx_j$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $R\to P\twoheadrightarrow B$, with ideal $I$. It gives an exact sequence $C\xrightarrow{u}V\to\Omega^1_{B/R}\to0$, whose last map sends $dx_j$ to $d\bar x_j$. Hence its induced map $\operatorname{coker}u\to\Omega^1_{B/R}$ is the required canonical isomorphism. For $a\in P$ the polynomial differential formula of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] gives the lift $v_a=\sum_j\overline{\partial a/\partial x_j}dx_j$ of $d\bar a$. No injectivity of $u$ is claimed or needed.

The immersion $\operatorname{Spec}B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A_R^{c+1}$ has its ideal generated by the Koszul-regular sequence established in step 1. Apply [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] to this factorization: its canonical conormal comparison identifies $E=[C\to V]$ with the intrinsic $L_{B/R}$ in the derived category, and is compatible with restriction. Its terms are finite free of ranks $c,c+1$. Thus [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] identifies its determinant with $D(E)$ and transports it to $\det L_{B/R}$. The degree-zero comparison is the cokernel map of step 2: the conormal model sends the differential of each polynomial generator to its universal differential, as specified by the natural presentation comparison in [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model].

Apply [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality] to the finite free two-term complex $E$ with ranks $c,c+1$, using the cokernel identification of step 2. Its stated existence and basis/lift independence give exactly $w:\Omega^1_{B/R}\to D(E)$ and the formula in the statement. Uniqueness holds because every element of the cokernel has a lift in $V$. Concretely, replacing a lift by $v+\sum_i b_i u(p_i)$ adds a sum of wedges with a repeated factor, hence zero; replacing $p$ by $pA$ multiplies its top wedge by $\det A$ and its dual by $(\det A)^{-1}$, which cancel. This also shows directly why no smoothness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed relation-first wedge formula; well-definedness supplied by the cited cofactor lemma, without applying a left-injectivity hypothesis.

proof.text: Put $p=p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_c$ and $q=dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c$. These are bases of the top exterior powers: multilinear expansion gives the permutation determinant as the coefficient of the ordered wedge, and the alternating coordinate determinant evaluates that wedge to $1$. Thus $p^\vee\otimes q$ is a basis of $D(E)$ and defines $e_0$. For $v_a$ from step 2, expand $u(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(p_c)\wedge v_a$. If $M$ has rows $(\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j})_j$ followed by $(\overline{\partial a/\partial x_j})_j$, terms with repeated column indices vanish and the remaining coefficient of $q$ is $\sum_{\sigma\in S_{c+1}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^{c+1}M_{i,\sigma(i)}=\det M$. Reduction $P\to B$ preserves this finite sum and products. Applying $e_0$ proves the augmented Jacobian formula with the stated row and column order.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula, expanded by multilinearity and alternation.

proof.text: For a principal open $D(b)$, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies the localized cokernel with $\Omega^1_{B_b/R}$. The formula and localization comparisons in [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent] say that $w\otimes_B B_b$ is precisely the cofactor map for $E\otimes_B B_b$. The conormal-to-intrinsic comparison restricts canonically by [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], and [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] identifies its determinant with the restriction of $D(E)$. On generators the wedge formula localizes coefficient by coefficient, so the same is true of $e_0$ and the determinant equality. Every open affine is covered by principal opens contained in it; the resulting equalities agree on their principal-open intersections and therefore give equality of the restricted sheaf maps. The intrinsic affine comparisons in the cotangent-presentation lemma identify these with the complexes on that affine. This proves restriction compatibility without assuming every affine open is itself principal.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:B\xrightarrow{\sim}B\prime$ be an isomorphism of the presented $R$-algebras. Transport scalars along $\varphi$; this is an equivalence, so it transports the displayed free modules and cokernel. By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], the standard intrinsic cotangent complex is functorial in this ring square and the inverse square, hence these maps are inverse derived isomorphisms. Compare any transported conormal model with a chosen model for $B\prime$ through these intrinsic isomorphisms and step 3. In degree zero the comparison is $d\bar a\mapsto d\varphi(\bar a)$. Indeed, write $B\prime=P\prime/I\prime$ with $P\prime$ polynomial over $R$; since $P$ is polynomial and $P\prime\to B\prime$ is surjective, choose $g_j\in P\prime$ lifting $\varphi(\bar x_j)$ and let $\psi:P\to P\prime$, $x_j\mapsto g_j$, a map of presentations over $\mathrm{id}_R$ and $\varphi$. By [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] the chain map $C(P)\to C(P\prime)$ sends $dx_j\otimes1$ to $dg_j\otimes1$ and commutes in $D$ with the standard functoriality map on $L$; under the cokernel maps of step 2 this is $d\bar x_j\mapsto d\varphi(\bar x_j)$, hence by $B$-linearity and the derivation rules of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it is the map $\Omega^1(\varphi)$, $d\bar a\mapsto d\varphi(\bar a)$, and $H^0(a)$ is this map. The equality $D(a)w_E=w_{E\prime}H^0(a)$ of [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality] now gives precisely transport compatibility. For literally transported ordered bases $e_0$ also transports, since its basis vector still maps to $1$; for different presentations the determinant comparison is the stipulated comparison of lines. Thus each augmented Jacobian expression represents the same intrinsic map, without asserting equality of unrelated scalar trivializations.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), standard-resolution maps; duality.tex Tag 0E9Y and more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM, via the cited intrinsic cofactor naturality.

proof.text: The ordered wedge throughout puts the $c$ relation differentials before the lifted differential, so it is relation-first, with the kernel-first normalization stipulated in [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality]. Passing to the corresponding shifted Koszul ordering only permutes these fixed-rank blocks and introduces the suspension signs fixed by their degrees. These signs depend on $c$ alone, not on coefficients, equations or $a$; hence the scalar trivialization changes only by such a sign. When $c=0$, the empty relation wedge and its dual are $1$, $C=0$, and the formula is $w(v)=v$. In particular $w(dx_0)=dx_0$, while the one-by-one augmented Jacobian is $\partial a/\partial x_0$, exactly the coefficient of $d\bar a$.
